title: Angular motion and the shared-arc ratio

board_content.text: $360$ revolutions per minute $= \frac{360}{60}=6$ revolutions per second. Each revolution is $2\pi$.
This ω in rad s⁻¹ feeds straight into v = rω in rotational mechanics.
Example 4 — equal arcs in two circles
Same arc: $r_1\theta_1 = r_2\theta_2$. The angles appear only as a ratio, so degrees are fine here.
Bigger angle on the same arc means a smaller radius — the inverse relationship is the trap.

segments_english.text: This example is the quiet bridge from maths straight into physics.
A wheel makes three hundred sixty revolutions in a minute. Per second that's three hundred sixty over sixty, which is six revolutions. Each revolution is two pi radians.
So the angular speed omega is six times two pi, that is twelve pi, about thirty seven point seven radians per second.
That omega, in radians per second, is exactly what plugs into v equals r omega for rim speed. Fumble the units here and you lose marks in rotational mechanics too.
The fourth example is a favourite ratio trap.

Two circles have arcs of equal length subtending sixty degrees and seventy five degrees at their centres. Since the arcs are equal, r one theta one equals r two theta two. The angles only appear as a ratio, so we can leave them in degrees, the conversion factor would cancel anyway.
So r one over r two equals theta two over theta one, which is seventy five over sixty, equal to five over four.
Read the meaning: a bigger angle sitting on the same arc means a tighter, smaller circle. Students who memorised s equals r theta but never felt it often flip this and write four to five.

segments_hinglish.text: ये example maths से सीधे physics में जाने वाला pul है.
एक wheel एक minute में तीन सौ साठ revolutions करता है. Per second ये three hundred sixty over sixty, यानी six revolutions. हर revolution two pi radians का है.
So angular speed omega है six times two pi, यानी twelve pi, करीब thirty seven point seven radians per second.
यही omega, radians per second में, exactly वही है जो v equals r omega में rim speed के लिए जाता है. Units यहाँ गड़बड़ की तो rotational mechanics में भी marks गए.
चौथा example एक favourite ratio trap है.

दो circles के arcs equal length के हैं, centres पर sixty और seventy five degrees बनाते हैं. Arcs equal हैं, so r one theta one equals r two theta two. Angles सिर्फ़ ratio में आते हैं, so degrees में छोड़ सकते हैं, conversion factor वैसे भी cancel हो जाता.
So r one over r two equals theta two over theta one, यानी seventy five over sixty, बराबर five over four.
मतलब समझिए: same arc पर बड़ा angle मतलब tighter, छोटा circle. जो s equals r theta रट लेते हैं पर feel नहीं करते वो अक्सर इसे उल्टा four to five लिख देते हैं.
